amended.suggestion: REVERSE GATE FAILURE (prereg S5-2 gate 2). The goal's last sentence -- 'Finally they want to eyeball a file from the shell without writing a script.' -- has NO check, visible or hidden. The contract does specify `python -m solution FILE` but adds 'Prints a table a person can read. Nothing about its layout is checked.', and no check in the bank spawns a subprocess for this task (ow_01 is the only task that does). The reference solution implements the CLI in ~16 of its 64 counted lines. As frozen, a worker who skips the CLI entirely loses nothing, and a worker who builds it is paying uncompensated difficulty -- exactly what gate 2 forbids ('留著＝在計分之外偷偷加難度'). Pick one: (a) add one hidden check that runs `python -m solution FILE` and asserts only exit 0 and non-empty stdout on a valid log, and exit non-zero on a missing file -- layout still ungraded; or (b) delete that sentence from goal.md and the whole 'Command line' section from contract.md. Do NOT leave it as it is. Author's choice; this reviewer does not edit the bank.

h12_written_order pins the exact emitted text, including the single spaces around '=' ('apple = 2'). Its declared anchor covers only the ORDER. The contract gives 'name = value' as a parse-side line grammar, and the reference parser accepts 'a=1', so a dumps that emits 'apple=2' satisfies every contract sentence -- both round-trip clauses included -- and still fails h12. Pick one: (a) add one contract sentence, e.g. '`dumps` writes each setting as `name = value`, with one space on each side of the `=`, and each heading on a line of its own.'; or (b) weaken h12 to assert the ORDER of names and headings (parse the written text, or compare stripped tokens) instead of the literal lines. (a) is preferable: the format is meant to be hand-editable, so pinning it is legitimate -- it simply is not pinned yet.

The goal gives three secrets as literal examples and says the client 'know[s] roughly what their secrets look like'. The hidden checks demand a generalisation the goal never states: h01 uses mysql://, h03 amqp://, h05 mongodb://, h06 redis:// where the goal shows only postgres://; h05 puts 'tok-one' after 'Authorization: Bearer' where the goal's example is a dot-separated JWT. Both visible checks, by contrast, use the goal's literal examples -- so a worker who hardcodes the three literals passes everything it can see and fails four of six hidden checks. Add one sentence to goal.md, e.g. 'The three lines above are shapes, not literals: the same kinds turn up with other key text, other token text, and other database schemes.' That makes the demand anchored; it does not make the task harder than it already is. (meta.json's own known_limitation already concedes the checks cannot tell a general scanner from a narrow one; this amendment is about the opposite direction -- the checks demanding more breadth than the goal states.)

h03_hyphen_rules asserts `slug != ""` for the title '...' (pure punctuation). The goal's non-empty guarantee is scoped to 'a title written in a script with no Latin letters in it at all', which does not clearly cover a title with no letters at all. Pick one: (a) widen the goal bullet to 'a title with nothing usable in it -- another script, or only punctuation -- still gets a non-empty slug'; or (b) drop the `slug != ""` assertion from h03 (h07 already carries the non-empty requirement where it is anchored). (a) is preferable: an empty slug is a real bug for the client and the property deserves to be graded.

NOT A CHECK ISSUE -- a rubric issue, raised because S5-2 is a spec-fairness review and S1-4 is part of what the prereg freezes. The three loose rubric.md files add a scoring weight that is nowhere in the prereg: 'blind score is readability + 2*structure + error_handling + 2*fit_to_goal', attributed to 'prereg amendment, Fable ruling 2026-09-13'. The prereg S1-4 says the rubric is shared by every task ('全部題目共用同一份') and no weighting appears anywhere in the document; S6-6 already fixes what the qualitative section may report (four dims plus a three-dim total excluding 'fit to goal'). A 2x weight on fit-to-goal also doubles the weight of the one dimension S1-4 warns is correlated with the quantitative outcome. Either Fable ratifies the weighting into the prereg before AMEND1, or the three loose rubrics drop it. It must not travel into AMEND1 citing a ruling the frozen document does not contain.

boundary_only_criteria_applied.rule: prereg S1-3b, three criteria, nothing else counts. A check is boundary_only=true only when EVERY input whose behaviour it grades falls under one of the three; a check that also grades an ordinary case is false.
boundary_only_criteria_applied.c1: the argument the function operates on is empty / zero-length ("", [], {}, None-as-no-file, a log with no lines, a file with no data rows).
boundary_only_criteria_applied.c2: the check's graded behaviour is an exception the contract requires.
boundary_only_criteria_applied.c3: an input value sits exactly on a boundary or extreme the contract names (window endpoint, rounding point, minimum legal value, unit step).
boundary_only_criteria_applied.sensitivity: The strict reading collapses largely onto criterion (2): 40 of the 55 are exception checks. Reading (1) as 'zero-length state' and (3) as 'near a named boundary' would add roughly 12 more (ow_02 h02/h08, ow_01 h04/h13, ow_03 h09, ow_05 h09/h15, ow_16 h03, ow_08 h04, ow_17 h06, ow_18 h06, ow_13 h13), i.e. ~27% instead of ~22%. The number is sensitive to the reading; prereg S1-3b says no threshold reads it, so this is descriptive only and must not be turned into a gate after the fact.
